strongest_angle: In October 2026, a Super El Niño event triggered massive rains that caused the Iguazú River to flow at six times its normal rate, forcing the temporary closure of Iguazú Falls on the Brazil-Argentina border and causing widespread flooding across Argentina, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

key_facts.fact: In October 2026, heavy rains linked to a Super El Niño caused the Iguazu River to flow at six times the normal rate, leading to the temporary closure of Iguazu Falls on the Brazil-Argentina border.
The Iguazu Falls form a complex of cascades spanning more than a mile across both Brazil and Argentina, which experienced near-record water volumes during the October 2026 rains.
Rivers swollen by heavy rains linked to El Niño continued flooding swaths of Argentina, Paraguay, and Uruguay in October 2026, forcing thousands of people from their homes.
